default.basis_text: two events of the same guns: the first fire, put at 3.30 (Geary) and 3.45 (Candy), at 4 a. m. (Packer, Greene, Slocum) and at 4.30 a. m. (Muhlenberg, Hunt), and the general fire, put at 5.30 a. m. by Hunt and Muhlenberg.

animation.note: The batteries open at the later end of the first-fire window, 04:30, the hour the commander of the guns and the chief of artillery give. That is not earlier than any source (Geary 3.30 and Candy 3.45 stay selectable, and are earlier). The general fire follows at 05:30. The infantry fight at Culp's Hill begins about 3 to 3.30 (Kane, Rickards).

default.note: The plan's two values are two events of the same guns, not rival values for one event: 05:30 is the general fire; the first fire is put between 03:30 and 04:30.

weighing.summary: The plan's 04:30 and 05:30 are both in Hunt's report and mean different things: at 4.30 the batteries Hunt had posted opposite the Twelfth Corps's centre fire fifteen minutes into the wood, and at 5.30, with Rigby's battery added, all the batteries open and fire at intervals to 10. So 05:30 is not a rival for the first fire. For the first fire the record is divided: Muhlenberg, who commanded the twenty guns, and Hunt say 4.30; Packer and Greene (eyewitnesses) and Slocum (the corps summary) say 4 a. m.; Geary has his division's attack by artillery and infantry at 3.30 (early dawn) with artillery fire for ten minutes, and Candy has a battery open on the enemy at 3.45; Williams has the artillery open at daylight for fifteen minutes. Geary and Candy describe the same bombardment, on the ground, within weeks, and rank with Greene and Packer, so they are not set aside: the first fire is the window 03:30 to 04:30, in the dark, when an hour is an estimate (sunrise 04:36). Nothing separates the readings, so the conflict is irreducible; the general fire at 5.30 is carried by Hunt and Muhlenberg alone.
weighing.who: Muhlenberg commanded the Twelfth Corps's artillery brigade, whose twenty guns opened; Hunt commanded the artillery of the army and posted the batteries. Greene commanded the infantry brigade whose line the guns fired across; Packer's regiment lay in reserve on the same crest; Slocum commanded the wing. Geary and Candy commanded the division and a brigade on the ground the guns shelled; Steuart held the works the guns shelled.
weighing.when: Candy wrote on 6 Jul 1863, Greene on 12 Jul, Packer on 21 Jul, Geary on 29 Jul, Williams on 22 Aug, Hunt on 27 Sep; Muhlenberg and Slocum in August, Steuart in 1863: all days to weeks after, none a diary of the day. They rank alike.
weighing.where: Muhlenberg and Hunt were at the guns or the army's artillery headquarters; Greene, Packer, Geary and Candy were on the infantry line the guns fired over, in the dark of the early morning, when an a. m. hour is an estimate; Slocum was at the corps headquarters on the hill, beside Knap's battery.
weighing.how_knew: Muhlenberg and Hunt give the hours of orders they gave (posted at 1 a. m., opened 4.30); Greene, Packer, Geary and Candy say what they saw; Slocum summarises his subordinates' reports; none says he looked at a watch. Hunt gives the same hour as Muhlenberg; his two batteries are part of the twenty guns Muhlenberg counts.
weighing.clock: All the Union writers; Steuart is Confederate. The Union and Confederate clocks reportedly differed by about 20 minutes; it is not applied. An hour-long spread among Union writers is not that difference; '4 a. m.' may be a round figure, and the dark makes an hour an estimate.
weighing.independence: The 4.30 hour rests on one line of knowledge (Muhlenberg; Hunt gives the same hour). The 4 a. m. hour rests on two eyewitness reports (Packer, Greene) and the corps commander's summary (Slocum), which may rest on Greene's. The 5.30 hour rests on Hunt and Muhlenberg together. Geary, Candy and Steuart are single witnesses.

source_panel_text: Union batteries on Culp's Hill, Jul 3: the first fire is put at 3.30 and 3.45 (Geary, Candy), 4 a.m. (Packer, Greene, Slocum) and 4.30 (Muhlenberg, who commanded the guns, and Hunt); all batteries opened at 5.30 (Hunt). So 04:30 and 05:30 are two events. Six other values are listed.

pdf_default.note: 05:30 is a true hour but it is the general fire, not the first fire; the plan's other value 04:30 is the first fire of the batteries Hunt placed (others put it at 04:00, 03:45 or 03:30). The plan treats them as rivals; they are two events, and both stay.

first_delegated.note: Two events (04:30 first fire, 05:30 general fire) holds. Its first event is 04:30 alone: Packer, Greene and Slocum put it at 4 a. m. and Geary and Candy earlier, so the first fire is a window of 03:30 to 04:30 (with Geary and Candy), and the conflict is irreducible rather than documented.

readers.note: Row 'Jul 3 ~04:30 [DAWN]' (Muhlenberg's and Kinzie's batteries open on the wood for about 15 minutes): first fire becomes the window 03:30 to 04:30; the 04:30 row stays as the later end. Row not edited here.

Row 'Jul 3 ~03:30 to 04:30' (Union artillery of five batteries, 24 guns per a soldier's letter, opens on Steuart's brigade for 30 minutes to several hours; accounts differ): the window of 03:30 to 04:30 for the first fire, and the 05:30 general fire, fit the Official Records; 24 guns is not in them (Muhlenberg has 20 guns).
Row 'Jul 3 ~01:00' (Muhlenberg's and Kinzie's batteries posted opposite the XII Corps centre): matches Hunt and Muhlenberg (1 a. m. on the 3d).

Row 'Jul 3 overnight' (Muhlenberg's batteries along the Pike, Rigby on Powers Hill, another on McAllister Hill): Hunt has Rigby's battery placed soon after daylight, not overnight; the place is the row's own gap, not this conflict's.
Row 'Jul 2 night' (Muhlenberg along the Pike; Rigby on Powers Hill): the posting of 1 a. m. on the 3d, not Jul 2 night; no hour change for this conflict.

Row 'Jul 3 ~05:00-05:30 (hour not given)' (Steuart's dawn attack; open gap; the dawn attack hour 04:30 Hunt vs 05:30): the Confederate infantry fight began about 3 to 3.30 a. m. (Kane, Rickards) and Steuart has the Union fire at about daylight; this resolution does not date Steuart's attack.
XII Corps row carries C-028 as 'Jul 3 04:30 artillery opens' in its key positions; the arrival gate (Jul 1 17:30) is not touched.

what_would_change_it: A diary or report of the morning of 3 July by an officer of Muhlenberg's, Kinzie's, Knap's or Winegar's battery or of Best's staff that gives the hour of the first round, or a report of the Confederate defenders (Johnson's staff, the First Maryland Battalion) that gives the hour the Union guns opened.
